title: Jesse Stone's band and Coleman Hawkins in Kansas City
summary: He mentions Jesse Stone's 17-piece band and recalls that Coleman Hawkins's family required a guardian to travel with him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Kansas City, all these fabulous people - and that goes for Jesse Stone too, because Jesse had been -
Wasn't he from Kansas City too?

He had 17 pieces. That's where Coleman Hawkins was worked after what's-his-name got him, after (Vincent) Gavin Bushell, San Juan... He was Coleman Hawkin's guardian because he could not leave home. Coleman could not leave home because the parents said, "You gotta." That's the way they did us, Milt. You had to have somebody around you. You know what they mean, you come out of that yourself. Your mother not going to let you leave unless somebody going to watch over you. "You mean to tell me you're going to Gary, Indiana; you're going to Milwaukee? What're you doing up there?" That's too far from home. She can't watch you with your newspaper route. So you had to have somebody to watch over you.
